import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')

Empty static project. Build game with index.html, styles, JS modules. Need a high-quality, complete playable SRPG: dark fantasy, many classes, complex battle system. Should be visually polished, mobile support.

Let me plan the game deeply.

**Game concept**: "Ashen Covenant" / "Grimoire of the Hollow Crown" — dark fantasy tactical RPG. Grid-based isometric-ish? Simpler: 2D tactical grid with layered sprites drawn via canvas, atmospheric effects.

Features to implement:
- Title screen with dark aesthetic, animated embers/fog.
- Campaign: 3-4 battles with story interludes, party progression.
- Grid map maybe 12x9 tiles, elevations? "Complex battle system": 
  - Turn order based on Speed (CT system like FFT). ATB accumulation - complex and true to FFT.
  - Facing/height? Z-level height affecting damage and movement. Could add terrain height 0-2 with elevation bonus.
  - Classes: Squire, Knight, Archer, Black Mage, White Mage, Thief, Dragoon, Necromancer, Paladin, Assassin, Summoner, Dark Knight. Many classes with abilities.
  - Job system: units can change class between battles, learn abilities via JP/levels. Keep manageable: roster of 6-8 units, class change UI between battles, abilities per class, JP progression.
  - Stats: HP, MP, PA, MA, SPD, MOV, JMP, Faith, Brave? Could include Brave/Faith for dark RPG (CT-like). Damage formulas.
  - Status effects: Poison, Burn, Blind, Silence, Slow, Haste, Regen, Protect, Shell, Sleep, Stop, Fear, Weaken, Bleed. 
  - Combat mechanics: facing (back attacks bonus), height bonus, elemental affinities (fire/ice/lightning/dark/holy), charge times for spells (CT casting), reaction abilities? Counters. Support abilities.
  - AI with behavior: target selection, healing, casting, movement pathfinding.
  - Items/consumables, gold, shop? Between battles: recruit/level, equip. Keep scope but rich.
  - Permadeath? Dark RPG — fallen units at 0 HP get "downed" and can be revived in battle; if battle ends they survive with injuries. Simpler: KO'd units removed, revive with Phoenix Ash.
- Controls: mouse/touch click to select, move, attack; keyboard shortcuts; camera pan maybe not needed if grid fits.
- UI: tactical HUD, turn order bar, unit info panel, action menu, combat forecast, floating damage text, log.
- Save to localStorage.

Architecture: vanilla JS modules. Canvas rendering with procedural sprites (drawn shapes) to avoid assets. High-quality dark art direction using CSS + canvas.

Given complexity, need careful code. Let's design data and systems.

Files:
- index.html
- css/style.css
- js/main.js (entry, screens)
- js/data.js (classes, abilities, items, enemies, maps, campaign)
- js/game.js (battle engine)
- js/render.js (canvas renderer)
- js/ui.js maybe.
Could keep modules moderately split.

Let's define grid render: square tiles 1x1 with height. Use canvas with tile size dynamic, pseudo-3D: draw top face offset by height*12px, side faces. Units drawn as stylized figures (hood, armor) with shadows. Nice.

Grid maps as arrays of tile definitions: {h: height, type:'stone'|'grass'|'water'|'lava'|'rubble'|'void'}, obstacles. Need maps 3-4.

Battle engine:
- Units have pos {x,y}, facing (0..3), CT, hp, mp.
- Turn order via CT: each tick, units gain CT += speed; when reaches 100, acts. Actually classic: each unit accumulates CT; when CT>=100, unit gets turn, CT -= 100. This gives speed-based ordering. Charge spells use CT countdown ticks.
- On unit's turn: can move within MOV using BFS considering height differences <= JMP, plus act (one action), then turn ends. Player controls; AI acts automatically.
- Height: attackers higher get +10% damage per level? Melee only within 1 tile and height diff <=1; ranged can shoot.
- Facing: unit faces last move direction or target; back attacks +25% damage, side +10%? Compute relative direction.
- Hit chance based on facing, height, speed, statuses; spells often 100%.
- Damage formulas: physical = PA * power/100 * (brave/100?) etc. Keep in data.

Abilities:
Each class has 3-5 abilities with MP cost, range, AoE, power, element, status, cast time.

Command menu: Attack (basic weapon), Abilities (submenu), Items, Wait/Defend, Flee (maybe not), End Turn.

Battle forecast when targeting a unit: show hit%, damage, counter.

AI: simple scoring; melee move to adjacent weakest; healers heal lowest ally; casters cast if in range; also avoid? Fine.

Victory conditions: defeat all enemies / boss. Defeat condition: all player units down or leader down. Story.

Between battles: Camp screen: roster, class change, ability learning (JP), shop equipment, save, next battle. Keep class change restricted by "class levels". Simpler: Units have level & JP; every class unlocked? "Many classes" — provide 12 classes, unlocked as campaign progresses, with JP costs to learn abilities. But building full job system is big. Let's implement:

Roster units: 6 named characters each with base stats and a "class" chosen from unlocked classes. Player can switch class freely at camp for any unlocked class; class mastery levels persist per unit-class (JP). Learning abilities costs JP earned in battle per unit (shared job points? per class JP). Abilities available: current class abilities learned. Plus basic Attack/Item. Equipment simplified to weapon + relic per unit? Maybe weapon upgrades in shop.

To keep manageable but complex: 
- Each unit has job levels per class (XP earned on class after battle), abilities learned stored per class. Simplify: JP is per unit, universal, and abilities from current class can be bought if level requirement met. Hmm.

Alternative simpler yet satisfying: Each class has a skill tree of 4-6 abilities unlocked by class level. Units gain class XP while using that class; leveling unlocks abilities automatically. Switching class keeps levels. That's clean. Plus stat growth per level based on class. We show "CLASS RANK" bar.

Core unit stats base by character + class modifiers + level growth. Upon level up choose? Auto stats.

Equipment: weapon changes attack power/element, armor adds HP/DEF. Shop sells 6 items with gold. Keep simple, automatic best? Give shop UI.

Battle count: Prologue + 3 chapters maybe 4 battles. Campaign story text. Each map distinct. Boss final. That's a lot of content but doable.

Need robust, tested via Playwright. Can't manually play fully, but write tests via node? We can run browser with Playwright CLI to screenshot and check console. Need make game self-testable maybe expose window.game. We can use playwright via CLI. Let's check installed playwright-cli.

Let me scope time: This is a large single build. I'll aim for ~2500-3500 lines total. Need ensure it runs.

Design specifics:

**Visual**: Full-screen dark UI. Background #07070b with fog. Title: "THE HOLLOW CROWN" subtitle "A Grim Tactical Chronicle". Serif display font from Google Fonts? Network may be available; better bundle no external dependency. Use CSS fonts: 'Cinzel' via Google fonts link — risky offline but fallback serif okay. I'd rather use local system serif "Georgia" for reliability. Could add @import but no. Use custom letterspaced serif.

Screens:
1. Title screen (menu: New Chronicle, Continue, How to Play).
2. Story screen with typewriter narration and continue.
3. Camp/Company screen (roster, class, shop, chronicle, deploy).
4. Battle screen.
5. Victory / defeat overlays, story transitions.
6. Codex/help modal.

**Battle mechanics detail**:

Unit object:
```
{
 id, name, side:'player'|'enemy', charId, classId,
 level, xp, hp, maxHp, mp, maxMp,
 base:{hp,mp,pa,ma,spd,mov,jmp},
 pos:{x,y}, facing, ct, statuses:{poison:{turns,power},...},
 abilities:[ids], classLevels:{}, inventory? 
}
```
Compute derived stats from class and level:
base stats per character * growth + class modifiers. e.g., level L: hp = base.hp + growth.hp*(L-1) + class.hp. Attack = base.pa + growth*... etc.

Class data:
```
{id:'squire', name:'Squire', desc, icon, color, weapon:'sword',
 stats:{hp:0,mp:0,pa:2,ma:0,spd:0,mov:0,jmp:0},
 growth:{hp:8,mp:2,pa:.8,ma:.5,spd:.4},
 abilities:[{id, name, desc, mp, range, aoe, power, element, type:'physical'|'magical'|'heal'|'buff', status, cast, target:'enemy'|'ally'|'self'|'tile', ...}]
}
```
Abilities defined globally keyed by id; class lists ability ids with unlock ranks 1..5. Could define ability objects inline in classes for ease.

12 classes:
1. Squire (basic) — Steel Slash, Guard Stance, Rally (buff PA)
2. Knight — Shield Bash (stun), Iron Wall (protect), Crushing Blow (armor break)
3. Archer — Aimed Shot (high crit), Rain of Arrows (AoE), Crippling Shot (slow)
4. Black Mage — Ember Lance (fire), Frost Nova (AoE ice slow), Thunderfall (lightning), Abyssal Bolt (dark)
5. White Mage — Mend (heal), Sanctuary (AoE heal), Purge (cleanse), Resurrect (revive)
6. Thief — Backstab (high dmg from behind), Mug (steal gold), Smoke Veil (evade buff), Pilfer? 
7. Dragoon — Jump (range 2-3 high dmg), Dragon's Roar (fear), Lance Pierce (line)
8. Necromancer — Drain (damage+heal), Bone Wall? summon skeleton (adds unit!), Curse (weaken), Soul Harvest (AoE dark)
9. Paladin — Holy Smite (holy), Aegis (shell/protect), Lay on Hands (heal), Judgment (AoE holy)
